title: TEST 3.2 - 30P - PHIÊN BẢN 2: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (16 CÂU CAM 21)
passageText:
Paragraph 1
In many countries in the West, hysteria about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) is everywhere. There seems to be no shortage of sensationalist news about how AI could cure diseases, accelerate human innovation and improve human creativity. Just looking at the media headlines, you might think that we are already living in a future where AI has infiltrated every aspect of society.

Paragraph 2
While it is undeniable that AI has opened up a wealth of promising opportunities, it has also led to the emergence of a mindset that can be best described as 'AI solutionism'. This is the philosophy that, given enough data, machine learning algorithms can solve all of humanity's problems. But, in fact, instead of supporting AI progress, this mindset actually jeopardises the value of machine intelligence by disregarding important AI safety principles and setting unrealistic expectations about what AI can really do for humanity.

Paragraph 3
In only a few years, AI solutionism has made its way from the technology evangelists' mouths in Silicon Valley in California to the minds of government officials and policymakers around the world. The pendulum has swung from the dystopian notion that AI will destroy humanity to the utopian belief that our algorithmic saviour is here.

Paragraph 4
We are now seeing governments pledge support to national AI initiatives and compete in a technological race to dominate the burgeoning machine-learning sector. While many politicians proclaim the transformative effects of the coming 'AI revolution', they fail to realise the complexity around deploying advanced machine learning systems in the real world.

Paragraph 5
One of the most promising varieties of AI technologies are neural networks. This form of machine learning is loosely modelled on the neuronal structure of the human brain, but on a much smaller scale. But what many politicians do not understand is that simply adding a neural network to a problem will not automatically mean that you'll find a solution. Similarly, adding a neural network to a system of government does not mean it will be instantaneously more inclusive or fair.

Paragraph 6
AI systems need a lot of data to function, but the public sector typically does not have the appropriate data infrastructure to support advanced machine learning. Most of the data remains stored in offline archives. The few digitised sources of data that exist tend to be buried in bureaucracy. More often than not, data is spread across different government departments that each require special permissions to be accessed. Above all, the public sector typically lacks the human talent with the right technological capabilities to fully reap the benefits of machine intelligence.

Paragraph 7
For these reasons, the sensationalism over AI has attracted many critics. Stuart Russell, a professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley, has long advocated a more sensible and realistic approach that focuses on simple everyday applications of AI instead of the hypothetical takeover by super-intelligent robots. Similarly, Rodney Brooks, professor of robotics at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, writes that 'almost all innovations in robotics and AI take far, far, longer to be really widely deployed than people in the field and outside the field imagine'.

Paragraph 8
One of the many difficulties in deploying machine learning systems is that AI is extremely susceptible to adversarial attacks. This means that a malicious AI can target another AI to make it behave in a certain way, such as forcing it to make wrong predictions. Many researchers have warned against the rolling out of AI without appropriate security standards and defence mechanisms. Still, AI security remains an often overlooked topic when machine learning systems are installed.

Paragraph 9
If we are to reap the benefits and minimise the potential harms of AI, we must start thinking about how machine learning can be meaningfully applied to specific areas of government, business and society. This means we need to have a discussion about AI ethics and the distrust that many people have towards machine learning.

Paragraph 10
Most importantly, we need to be aware of the limitations of AI and where people still need to take the lead. Instead of painting an unrealistic picture of the power of AI, it is important to take a step back and separate the actual technological capabilities of AI from fantasy.

Paragraph 11
The medical profession has also recognised the drawbacks to AI. The IBM Watson for Oncology programme was a piece of AI that was meant to help doctors treat cancer. Even though it was developed to deliver the best recommendations, human experts found it hard to trust the machine. As a result, the AI programme was abandoned in most hospitals where it was trialled.

Paragraph 12
Similar difficulties arose in the legal domain when algorithms were used in courts in the US to sentence criminals. An algorithm calculated risk assessment scores and advised judges on the sentencing. The system was found to amplify structural racial discrimination and was later abandoned.

Paragraph 13
There are some crucial lessons here for everyone aiming to boost investments in national AI programmes. These examples demonstrate that there is no AI solution for everything. Using AI simply for the sake of AI may not always be productive or useful, and not every issue is best addressed by applying machine intelligence to it. All solutions come with a cost and not everything that can be automated should be.

questions.questionText: Many politicians overestimate neural networks, believing that their mere addition will produce solutions and promote [1] _______________ in government systems. (Choose from list: A. reliability | B. funding | C. skills | D. prejudices | E. computers | F. equality | G. framework | H. confidentiality | I. approval)
questions.evidenceQuote: Similarly, adding a neural network to a system of government does not mean it will be instantaneously more inclusive or fair.
questions.rubricGuide: Cặp tính từ 'more inclusive or fair' (hòa nhập và công bằng hơn) đồng nghĩa với danh từ 'equality' (sự bình đẳng/công bằng xã hội) -> F.

questions.questionText: Most public sector organisations have not set up the necessary [2] _______________ to manage the huge amount of data required. (Choose from list A - I)
questions.evidenceQuote: ...the public sector typically does not have the appropriate data infrastructure to support advanced machine learning.
questions.rubricGuide: Cụm 'appropriate data infrastructure' (cơ sở hạ tầng dữ liệu) đồng nghĩa với 'framework' (khung sườn/hạ tầng cơ sở) -> G.

questions.questionText: Complex bureaucracy is another issue, as each person involved needs [3] _______________ to access relevant data spread across departments. (Choose from list A - I)
questions.evidenceQuote: ...data is spread across different government departments that each require special permissions to be accessed.
questions.rubricGuide: Từ 'special permissions' (sự cho phép đặc biệt) đồng nghĩa với 'approval' (sự phê chuẩn / cho phép) -> I.

questions.questionText: The main problem is that few public sector employees have the [4] _______________ to take full advantage of machine intelligence. (Choose from list A - I)
questions.evidenceQuote: ...the public sector typically lacks the human talent with the right technological capabilities to fully reap the benefits of machine intelligence.
questions.rubricGuide: Cụm 'human talent with the right technological capabilities' (nhân tài có năng lực công nghệ) tương ứng với 'employees have the skills' -> C.

questions.questionText: Stuart Russell's proposals regarding the use of AI are impractical.
questions.evidenceQuote: Stuart Russell, a professor of computer science at the University of California, Berkeley, has long advocated a more sensible and realistic approach...
questions.rubricGuide: Đề bảo đề xuất của Russell là phi thực tế ('impractical'), trong khi bài khen là 'sensible and realistic' (hợp lý và thực tế). Hai ý trái ngược nhau 100% -> NO.

questions.questionText: Rodney Brooks' view has attracted unfair criticism from supporters of AI.
questions.evidenceQuote: Similarly, Rodney Brooks, professor of robotics at Massachusetts Institute of Technology, writes that 'almost all innovations in robotics and AI take far, far, longer to be really widely deployed than people in the field and outside the field imagine'.
questions.rubricGuide: Bài chỉ dẫn lời của Brooks về tiến độ triển khai AI, hoàn toàn không nhắc tới việc ông có bị người ủng hộ AI chỉ trích bất công ('unfair criticism') hay không -> NOT GIVEN.

questions.questionText: Nowadays, the need to protect AI systems is always taken into account when they are set up.
questions.evidenceQuote: Still, AI security remains an often overlooked topic when machine learning systems are installed.
questions.rubricGuide: Đề bảo bảo vệ an ninh AI luôn luôn được tính đến ('always taken into account'), bài khẳng định nó thường xuyên bị ngó lơ/bỏ qua ('often overlooked'). Mâu thuẫn trực tiếp -> NO.

questions.questionText: In order to benefit from AI and minimise the harms, we have to explore people's concerns about its use.
questions.evidenceQuote: If we are to reap the benefits and minimise the potential harms of AI... This means we need to have a discussion about AI ethics and the distrust that many people have towards machine learning.
questions.rubricGuide: Cụm 'have a discussion about... distrust that many people have' đồng nghĩa với 'explore people's concerns' (tìm hiểu quan ngại/sự ngờ vực của người dân). Trùng khớp 100% -> YES.

questions.questionText: Which paragraph contains a reference to a situation where an algorithm perpetuated societal bias in legal decisions?
questions.evidenceQuote: Similar difficulties arose in the legal domain when algorithms were used in courts in the US to sentence criminals... The system was found to amplify structural racial discrimination and was later abandoned.
questions.rubricGuide: Đoạn 12 kể về việc thuật toán tòa án Mỹ khuếch đại nạn phân biệt chủng tộc mang tính cấu trúc ('amplify structural racial discrimination' = perpetuated societal bias).

questions.questionText: Which paragraph contains an explanation of why adding machine learning to governance fails to ensure immediate fairness?
questions.evidenceQuote: Similarly, adding a neural network to a system of government does not mean it will be instantaneously more inclusive or fair.
questions.rubricGuide: Đoạn 5 giải thích việc đưa mạng nơ-ron vào chính quyền không đồng nghĩa với việc nó sẽ ngay lập tức hòa nhập hoặc công bằng hơn ('instantaneously more inclusive or fair').

questions.questionText: Which paragraph contains a description of the vulnerability of machine learning systems to targeted interference?
questions.evidenceQuote: One of the many difficulties in deploying machine learning systems is that AI is extremely susceptible to adversarial attacks. This means that a malicious AI can target another AI to make it behave in a certain way...
questions.rubricGuide: Đoạn 8 mô tả điểm yếu của AI khi rất dễ bị tấn công đối kháng ('susceptible to adversarial attacks' = vulnerability to targeted interference).

questions.questionText: Which paragraph contains a mention of a failed medical AI deployment due to skepticism among healthcare professionals?
questions.evidenceQuote: The medical profession has also recognised the drawbacks to AI. The IBM Watson for Oncology programme... human experts found it hard to trust the machine. As a result, the AI programme was abandoned...
questions.rubricGuide: Đoạn 11 nói về dự án IBM Watson điều trị ung thư bị hủy bỏ vì các chuyên gia bác sĩ không dám đặt niềm tin vào máy tính ('found it hard to trust' = skepticism).

questions.questionText: What is the writer doing in the first paragraph?
options: A. Predicting the future impact of AI.
B. Describing a public perception of AI.
C. Outlining some possible benefits of AI.
D. Highlighting the breadth of the influence of AI.
questions.evidenceQuote: In many countries in the West, hysteria about the future of artificial intelligence (AI) is everywhere... Just looking at the media headlines, you might think that we are already living in a future...
questions.rubricGuide: Tác giả mô tả cách công chúng và báo chí nhìn nhận về AI qua các từ 'hysteria', 'sensationalist news', 'you might think' -> miêu tả nhận thức của dư luận ('describing a public perception').

questions.questionText: When discussing AI solutionism in the second paragraph, the writer
options: A. points out a risk involved.
D. weighs up some pros and cons.
questions.evidenceQuote: ...this mindset actually jeopardises the value of machine intelligence by disregarding important AI safety principles and setting unrealistic expectations...
questions.rubricGuide: Từ 'jeopardises' (gây nguy hiểm/đe dọa) và 'disregarding safety' (bỏ qua an toàn) chính là việc chỉ ra một rủi ro tiềm ẩn ('points out a risk involved').

questions.questionText: In the fourth paragraph, the writer suggests that many politicians may
options: A. have failed to appreciate the true potential of AI initiatives.
B. have misunderstood the function of the machine-learning sector.
C. be unaware of the challenges of implementing national AI initiatives.
D. be too keen to enter the race to dominate the machine-learning sector.
questions.evidenceQuote: While many politicians proclaim the transformative effects of the coming 'AI revolution', they fail to realise the complexity around deploying advanced machine learning systems in the real world.
questions.rubricGuide: Cụm 'fail to realise the complexity' (không nhận ra sự phức tạp) đồng nghĩa với 'be unaware of the challenges' (không ý thức được thách thức khi triển khai).

questions.questionText: What would be a suitable subtitle for Reading Passage 3?
options: A. How to make the most of what AI has to offer.
B. Why AI may not be the answer to our problems.
C. Why governments should not invest in AI systems.
D. How AI could improve the efficiency of the public sector.
questions.evidenceQuote: These examples demonstrate that there is no AI solution for everything. Using AI simply for the sake of AI may not always be productive or useful, and not every issue is best addressed by applying machine intelligence to it.
questions.rubricGuide: Thông điệp kết luận toàn bài: 'there is no AI solution for everything' (không có giải pháp AI cho mọi thứ) tương ứng với 'Why AI may not be the answer to our problems'.
